repo.description:
> [!NOTE]
> **Fixed in Logto 1.46.0** (https://github.com/logto-io/logto/commit/0d7eeedf49dff7496de933d015d3a0b4b55b247b). Changing the interaction event now discards the identified user, together with the MFA factors staged for them and their trusted-device opt-in, so an interaction switched from sign-in to registration can no longer finish without the second factor. An email or phone MFA challenge is also bound to the user it was created for.
>
> Upgrade to 1.46.0; no configuration change is needed. The MFA policy setting does not mitigate this on earlier versions. Until you can upgrade, setting the sign-in mode to sign-in only (registration disabled) blocks the event switch.
>
> GHSA-f78f-ghjf-hrx2 covers a related gap in the same check and is also fixed in 1.46.0.

---

## Summary

MFA bypass: switching interaction event SignIn→Register after identification skips second-factor verification

## Affected code

`packages/core/src/routes/experience/classes/experience-interaction.ts`:546

experience-interaction.ts:545-548 (the flawed gate):
545  // Verified, only SignIn requires MFA verification, for register, it does not make sense to verify MFA
546  if (this.#interactionEvent === InteractionEvent.SignIn) {
547    await this.guardMfaVerificationStatus(log);
548  }

experience-interaction.ts:192-211 (event switch keeps the identified user; only profile is cleared):
206  if (this.#interactionEvent !== interactionEvent) {
207    this.profile.cleanUp();
208  }
209  this.#interactionEvent = interactionEvent;   // this.userId is never reset

experience-interaction.ts:229-265 (identifyUser sets userId; only blocks the Register event at entry, so it runs under SignIn):
230  assertThat(this.interactionEvent !== InteractionEvent.Register, new RequestError({ code: 'session.invalid_interaction_type', status: 400 }));
264  this.userCache = user;
265  this.userId = id;

sign-in-experience-validator.ts:114-122 (switch to Register allowed whenever registration is enabled):
114  case InteractionEvent.Register: {
115    assertThat(signInMode !== SignInMode.SignIn || hasVerifiedOneTimeToken, new RequestError({ code: 'auth.forbidden', status: 403 }));

mfa.ts:520-529 (residual Register-time check only requires factors BOUND, not verified):
521  assertThat(
522    configuredFactors.some((factor) => linkedFactors.includes(factor)),
523    new RequestError({ code: 'user.missing_mfa', status: 422 }, ...)
524  );

index.ts:101-126 (the PUT /experience/interaction-event route with no re-identification/MFA guard):
118  await experienceInteraction.setInteractionEvent(interactionEvent);

Corroborating test - an existing identified user under a Register event submits successfully with no MFA verification (experience-interaction.test.ts:345-354): createSignInInteraction({ interactionEvent: InteractionEvent.Register }) with userId = existing mockUser, then experienceInteraction.submit() resolves.

## Attacker model

An unauthenticated attacker who knows only the victim's password (the first factor). No bearer token, no admin, no second factor. They drive their own OIDC sign-in interaction (they hold the interaction cookie from PUT /api/experience). Requires the tenant to have registration enabled (signInMode = SignInAndRegister, the Logto default) and password sign-in enabled.

## Details

ExperienceInteraction.submit() only verifies the user's second factor (MFA) when the interaction event is SignIn: `if (this.#interactionEvent === InteractionEvent.SignIn) { await this.guardMfaVerificationStatus(log); }` (experience-interaction.ts:546-548). The comment on line 545 states the assumption 'for register, it does not make sense to verify MFA' - i.e., the code assumes a Register submit is always a brand-new user. That assumption is violated: an attacker can (1) identify an EXISTING victim under a SignIn interaction using only the password (identifyUser sets this.userId = victim, experience-interaction.ts:264-265), then (2) call PUT /api/experience/interaction-event to switch the event to Register. setInteractionEvent (experience-interaction.ts:192-211) keeps this.userId intact - it only calls profile.cleanUp() (lines 206-208) and never clears the identified user; guardInteractionEvent permits the switch whenever signInMode !== SignIn (sign-in-experience-validator.ts:114-122). Now submit() runs the Register branch: guardMfaVerificationStatus (the ONLY place a verified MFA verification record is required) is skipped. The residual MFA check, mfa.assertMfaFulfilled() -> assertUserMandatoryMfaFulfilled (mfa.ts:520-529), only asserts that the required factors are BOUND to the account (`configuredFactors.some(factor => linkedFactors.includes(factor))`, where linkedFactors is derived from the victim's existing user.mfaVerifications), NOT that any second factor was verified in this interaction. A victim who has MFA configured passes this trivially. submit() then calls provider.interactionResult({ login: { accountId: victim.id } }) (experience-interaction.ts:670-674), completing OIDC login as the victim. Net effect: password-only login despite mandatory MFA.

## Proof of concept

**Entrypoint:** `Experience API (interaction-session cookie, anonymous end-user mid-sign-in): PUT /api/experience, POST /api/experience/verification/password, POST /api/experience/identification, PUT /api/experience/interaction-event, POST /api/experience/submit`

1. POST/PUT /api/experience  body {"interactionEvent":"SignIn"}  (creates interaction, obtains interaction cookie).
2. POST /api/experience/verification/password  body {"identifier":{"type":"username","value":"<victim>"},"password":"<victim password>"}  -> {verificationId}. The password record is now verified.
3. POST /api/experience/identification  body {"verificationId":"<verificationId>"}  -> 204. identifyUser() runs under SignIn (allowed), sets interaction.userId = victim's id. No MFA performed yet (MFA is only checked at submit).
4. PUT /api/experience/interaction-event  body {"interactionEvent":"Register"}  -> 204. setInteractionEvent(Register) succeeds because signInMode is SignInAndRegister; this.userId (victim) is preserved, only the staged profile is cleared.
5. POST /api/experience/submit  -> 200 {redirectTo}. submit() takes the non-SignIn path: guardMfaVerificationStatus is NOT called; assertUserMandatoryProfileFulfilled passes (victim already has all mandatory profile fields); assertMfaFulfilled passes because the victim already has the required MFA factor bound. provider.interactionResult logs in accountId = victim. Following the returned redirectTo completes the OIDC flow and issues tokens for the victim.
Result: full authenticated session as the victim using only the password, with MFA (TOTP/WebAuthn/backup-code/email/phone second factor) never verified.

## Impact

Complete bypass of multi-factor authentication for any MFA-enrolled account whose password is known/compromised. This defeats the exact control MFA exists to provide (protection against a compromised password), yielding full account takeover: a valid OIDC session and tokens for the victim, including access to any first-party app and the account-management (Account Center) surface. Works under Mandatory as well as optional/user-controlled MFA policies, and does not require the victim to interact.

## Verification notes

Claim's mfa.ts citation "520-529" is off by one: the assertThat begins at line 521 and the configuredFactors.some(...) is at line 522 (file read confirms). All experience-interaction.ts (546-548, 206-210, 230-265) and sign-in-experience-validator.ts (114-122) citations are accurate. The residual-check semantics, event-switch preservation of userId, and single-call-site of the in-interaction MFA verification are all confirmed as described.
repo.summary: MFA bypass: switching interaction event SignIn→Register after identification skips second-factor verification
